line: Run up on a nigga like bang bang Get you popped right now Make a nigga go meet ’Pac right now
vault_lines: Run up on a nigga like bang bang
meaning:
This is my flip of Jay Z’s line from “Friend or Foe ‘98” when he said:

Take that ice up for the nicest MC
And please yo, tell BIG he’s unbelievable

I just did it in my own little way.

line: Brat, brat, brat, brat, Free Bobby, bitch!
vault_lines: Brat, brat, brat, brat, Free Bobby, bitch!
meaning:
I think it was a real unfortunate situation when Bobby and Rowdy got locked up. They were just some young niggas from the hood that found a way out.

I think the police tried to stick it to them. I think they had a strong influence on what was going on in music and I don’t know if the police didn’t like that, but it’s an unfortunate situation.

I hope they get over that situation and get out that shit.

line: Young Metro don’t trust you, I’m gon shoot you
vault_lines: Young Metro don't trust you, I'm gon shoot you
meaning:
I’m not gonna lie, I definitely didn’t know this line was going to be as big as it is right now.

Young Metro did an interview and let people know that the origins of this line was from “Right Now.”

Now it’s on Kanye’s TLOP record and on all these memes, it’s dope.

line: If Future don’t trust ya Bang bang, hit you in the head right now
meaning:
When I recorded this line, Future already laid his “If Murda don’t trust you I'ma shoot you” line down.

He set me up for me to do this line.

line: Scheme on it, I drop a bag and get you hit right now My bread right now Can’t tell me I can’t beat the Feds right now
vault_lines: Scheme on it, I drop a bag and get you hit right now
meaning:
One day I was just counting up $100,000 and I was feeling good about it. So when I was writing the song, the memory just popped in my head.

I come from eating peanut butter sandwiches and drinking Kool-Aid, now a nigga is eating in 5-Star restaurants.

Then if you don’t have your money right for a lawyer and you go against the Feds, you’re gonna take that L.

Their conviction rate is crazy.

line: I’m lit right now Bitch, recognize who you with right now I’m the shit right Look at the flick of the wrist right now This Audemars cost the price of a New York brick right now
meaning:
This a reference to this nice audemar watch that’s on my wrist. And when you’re whipping that work as well, when you’re stirring that thing in the pot trying to get a little bit of extra.

The audemar that I’m rocking is about $40,000, and anybody that’s in the streets right now knows that the price for a New York brick is about 40 bands.

There’s a couple of different influences with this line. The Chedda Da Connect record is also an influence, I like that how that record sounds.

line: Oh, I just got some pounds from the plug If you ain’t gettin’ money, you a dub
vault_lines: Oh, I just got some pounds from the plug
meaning:
Nowadays if you ain’t getting money you might as well be dead.

Dub, that’s the new thing. It means you’re dead, get out of here, it’s over for you.

line: I got your bitch on 5th ave, I’m Daddy
vault_lines: I got your bitch on 5th ave, I'm Daddy
meaning:
Sometimes the ladies deserve it. Sometimes they work hard and you go, “You know what, you could go on 5th Ave today.”

You could always take them to the Louis Vuitton spot, but just make sure you get her a Chanel bag. If you get a female a Chanel bag it will go a long way.

line: I’m strapped right now Even police get clapped right now
meaning:
I’ve been real vocal about the police and the negative things they’ve been doing forever, since I first came out.

Now, the negative stuff that the police have been doing is more in the public’s eye. Sometimes I just like to vent. I’m not saying we’ll really go out there and do that, but I just be venting because the police do so much bullshit.

Being on a record with Future, I wanted to highlight how I feel about them motherfuckers sometimes. I had to sneak that in there because I knew the record would get a lot of play. I wanted people to hear it.

line: Niggas in the club right now Bitches gettin’ high on drugs right now Got shooters on deck, I call Crips, call Bloods right now Real niggas back, I’m puttin’ on for my hittas
vault_lines: Niggas in the club right now
meaning:
When we were doing the record in the studio In L.A., there were Crips in the studio with us and there were Bloods in the studio.

My nigga Reed was there and Game and Wack were in the other studio right next to us. Then they left and there were some Loc homies in there too.

line: Headshots, trap money The streets watchin’, but they ain’t trippin’ If money come this fast, I swear to God I never spend it
vault_lines: The streets watchin', but they ain't trippin'
meaning:
The term “the streets is watching” was popularized in rap when Jay Z dropped his 1997 song “Streets is Watching.”

The term basically means that the streets see everything. If you’re getting illegal money in the trap, someone may just shoot you for it.

Future isn’t worried though, he’s going to continue to make his money fast and spend it just as quickly.

line: Break a whole brick down Look at all of these baggies
meaning:
A “brick” of cocaine is pure, uncut product, usually weighing a kilogram, or 2.2 pounds. A dealer will receive their cocaine in this form, before cutting it (or breaking it down) with substances like baking soda to increase the weight and street value.



Murda has already talked about “whippin'” his drugs, so he’s likely producing crack cocaine, a product that delivers a quicker, more intense high due to the inclusion and “cooking” of other ingredients. He’s planning on distributing it in zip lock baggies.

line: We blowin’ money, we throwin’ money at strippers Niggas in the trap right now Whippin’ it ’til it come back right now
vault_lines: We blowin' money, we throwin' money at strippers
meaning:
“Whippin'” in the trap house refers to cooking up crack cocaine, ready for sale. The money made from cooking crack is funding Murda’s strip club escapades: he’s making it rain dirty money.



The process of cooking crack involves dissolving the mixture in water until it solidifies and floats to the top. It “disappears” in the liquid before coming right back.

Jay Z rapped about the process on his 2014 track “Crown.”

You already know what I could do with the coke
Dropped it in the water, made it disappear
I made it reappear, I had that bitch on a rope

line: I just blow the cash on my young ho I just blow some cash on my young ho Fuckin’ up this cash with my young niggas Fuckin’ up a bag with my young niggas
vault_lines: I just blow the cash on my young ho
meaning:
To “blow cash” or to “fuck up a bag” means to spend money frivolously— it’s a recurring theme in Future’s music.

On “Blow A Bag” and his certified gold single “Fuck Up Some Commas” Future raps about his reckless spending habits.

But Future isn’t selfish, he doesn’t just buy lavish gifts for himself but for his homies and women friends as well.

vault_lines: Metro Boomin want some more, nigga
meaning: One of Metro’s producer tags, spat by Young Thug on “Some More,” and popularized by the multiple hits he’s concocted for Future over the past few years.

line: Niggas in the club right now Blowin’ on kush, gettin’ money right now Niggas wanna play right now Got jewels, got cars, got shooters right now
vault_lines: Niggas in the club right now
meaning:
With the intro Future sets the scene. He’s in the club, smoking weed and getting money. While most folks have to pay to get into the club, Future gets paid very well to party.

In 2013 it was reported Future was paid $45,000 to appear at a Las Vegas nightclub.

line: Brat, brat, brat, brat, Free Rowdy, bitch!
vault_lines: Brat, brat, brat, brat, Free Rowdy, bitch!
meaning: Rowdy Rebel is a Brooklyn rapper who was arrested on December 17, 2014, on charges of conspiracy, attempted murder, attempted assault, reckless endangerment and criminal possession of a weapon. Rowdy was arrested along with Bobby Shmurda the GS9 Crew, which Rowdy was part of.

line: If Murda don’t trust you, he gon’ shoot you Lil’ Mexico don’t trust you, we gon shoot you
vault_lines: If Murda don't trust you, he gon' shoot you
meaning:
Murda and Future are clicked up, only giving a pass on violence to those outside their crew that are trusted by members of the crew.

“Lil' Mexico"—also known as Kirkwood—is a hood in East Atlanta where Future is from. Murda is from Brooklyn.
